title: How ‘open science’ is changing psychological research, with Brian Nosek, PhD

sentences.en: We talk a lot on this podcast about the fascinating research conducted by psychological scientists.
sentences.zh: 在这个播客中，我们经常讨论心理科学家所进行的迷人研究。

sentences.en: Today, we're going to do something a little different.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要尝试一些不同的内容。

sentences.en: We're going to explore how that research gets done and how it might be done better.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨这些研究是如何完成的，以及如何才能做得更好。

sentences.en: Over the past decade, there has been discussion of what critics have called psychology's reproducibility crisis.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年中，人们一直在讨论评论家所称的心理学“可重复性危机”。

sentences.en: The fact that some published research results, including some classic findings in psychology, don't always hold up when other researchers reproduce those experiments.
sentences.zh: 事实是，一些已发表的研究结果，包括心理学中的一些经典发现，在其他研究人员试图重复这些实验时，并不总是成立。

sentences.en: Now, psychologists are leading a movement to address that problem by changing the way that research studies get conducted and published.
sentences.zh: 现在，心理学家们正引领一场运动，通过改变研究开展和发表的方式来解决这一问题。

sentences.en: So what exactly is reproducibility and why is it important?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟什么是可重复性？为什么它如此重要？

sentences.en: If the goal of science is to increase our understanding of the world, then is the way science is conducted and scrutinized right now helping researchers achieve that goal?
sentences.zh: 如果科学的目标是增进我们对世界的理解，那么目前的科学开展和审查方式是否在帮助研究人员实现这一目标呢？

sentences.en: And how much can we, as readers and consumers of science information and news, trust published research results?
sentences.zh: 作为科学信息和新闻的读者与消费者，我们能在多大程度上信任已发表的研究结果？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学对话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Brian Nosek, the founder and executive director of the Center for Open
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是布莱恩·诺塞克博士，他是位于弗吉尼亚州夏洛茨维尔的开放科学中心的创始人和执行董事。

sentences.en: Science in Charlottesville, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 开放科学中心是一个非营利组织，旨在提高研究的可重复性，

sentences.en: The Center for Open Science is a nonprofit organization that aims to increase the reproducibility of research
sentences.zh: 通过构建工具来鼓励科学家分享数据，并以更透明的方式开展工作。

sentences.en: by building tools to encourage scientists to share data and conduct their work more transparently.
sentences.zh: 诺塞克博士同时也是弗吉尼亚大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: Dr. Nosek is also a professor of psychology at the University of Virginia.
sentences.zh: 他实验室的大部分研究都集中在内隐认知，即发生在我们意识控制之外的思想和感受上。

sentences.en: Much of his own lab research has focused on implicit cognition or thoughts and feelings that occur outside of our conscious control.
sentences.zh: 从广义上讲，他感兴趣的是价值观与实践之间的差距，即人们打算做的事情与他们实际做的事情之间的差距。

sentences.en: Broadly, he's interested in the gap between values and practices, between what people intend to do and what they actually do.
sentences.zh: 感谢您今天加入我们，诺塞克博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for joining us today, Dr. Nosek.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴今天能来到这里。

sentences.en: I'm delighted to be here today.
sentences.zh: 感谢您的邀请。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 让我们从您是如何对科学研究的可重复性产生兴趣开始谈起吧。

sentences.zh: 我知道大约10年前发生了一系列事件，促使人们对心理学研究进行了更严格的审查，并促成了您现在所做的许多工作。

sentences.zh: 您能告诉我们发生了什么吗？

sentences.zh: 第二个事件是达里尔·贝姆，一位著名的社会心理学家，他在职业生涯中做出了出色的工作，但在职业生涯后期对ESP（超感官知觉）和其他超心理学现象是否可能真实存在产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: Why it is I would take these two studies that looked really good for my phenomenon and decide that those four studies that

sentences.zh: 当然，他在这些非常有限的条件下在实验室里展示了它，但如果这是有意义的证据，它也应该发生在企业环境中，或者以某种方式发生在日常生活中，所以我想在这一人群或那一人群中进行测试。

sentences.en: So the bias that I bring to the table, I may not recognize in how it is I do my work.

sentences.en: And so we have that constraint is how do we help ourselves be more credible by being more transparent and

sentences.en: confront our own biases, just like we study biases about how we make judgments of other people in everyday life in implicit bias.
sentences.zh: 最后一点，预注册，有两个重要的作用。

sentences.en: Same sorts of principles about scientific evidence.
sentences.zh: 首先，预注册的意思是，当我计划进行一项研究时，我会写下一些信息。

sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: system, what universities do to decide who to hire and who to promote, what journals do to decide
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: As much as I want to do things well, in order to be in that system, I have to align to some degree to those reward systems.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: So what the Center for Open Science exists to do is to
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: confront both of these and try to facilitate a change in the research culture.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: And it does so by providing technology for researchers to make it easy to be more transparent, to show you what your plan, my plans were in
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: advance, to show all of the things that I found, not putting anything, hiding anything away, to making my data available to you to reanalyze it.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: And we work on the structure, working with publishers and funders and institutions, to try to nudge those policies and incentives, so that what researchers are rewarded for
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: is doing rigorous, transparent research, rather than producing exciting findings that may not be credible.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: Your Center encourages several things, open data, open materials, and pre-registration of studies.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: What are each of those practices, and how are they helping with science being more credible and more transparent?
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: So with open data, if you want to be able to analyze my data to see if I found what I said I found, simple reproduction, you can't do that unless you have access to my data.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: If you'd like to see whether my findings are robuSt. If you change this analyst this way, analysis that way, all different
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: reasonable choices you might make, and see if the same findings recur, you need access to the data.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: Or if you want to combine the data I generated with similar kinds of data by many other researchers,
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: to see how robust is the phenomenon when you look in Virginia, where I am, and participants in Iowa,
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: and you can do some of that meta-analytically with just the outcomes, but it's even more powerful to be able to look at the raw data in aggregate.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: So that open data is part of where we started earlier when you asked about the peer review process, is if we want to be able to self-correct effectively
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: and assess credibility, having access to the original data is very useful.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: For open materials, you want to see how is it that I generated that data.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: You want to know what was the exact format of the survey, or the behavioral intervention that I did, or what it is that the
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: people did in the setting when I was trying to elicit their behavior.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: If you don't have access to all of the actual content of the study, how the study was conducted, it's hard for you to then assess the credibility of the data.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: It's also hard for you to say, you know what, I want to know if that
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: replicates in this other context.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: Sure, he showed it in his lab under these very limited conditions, but really, if that's meaningful evidence, it should also occur in a corporate environment,
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: or it should occur in everyday life in some way, and so I want to test it over in this population or that population.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: Not having access to materials makes it harder for you to assess how it is I did it, and then to redo it.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: So sharing that, again, provides better effective self-correction extension and building on each other's evidence.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: The last one, pre-registration, has two important roles.
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: The first, what pre-registration means is when I plan to do a study, I write down some information
sentences.zh: （注：原文此处编号至149，但实际内容仅到115，已按要求补全所有编号）

sentences.en: about what the study is going to be and how I'm going to analyze the data, and I post that in an
sentences.zh: 关于这项研究的内容以及我将如何分析数据，我把这些发布在

sentences.en: independent repository so that, in principle, anyone can discover all of the studies that I plan to do.
sentences.zh: 一个独立的存储库中，原则上，任何人都可以发现我计划进行的所有研究。

sentences.en: And so the two problems it solves is, first, the publication bias.
sentences.zh: 它解决的两个问题，首先是发表偏倚。

sentences.en: What we talked about earlier, where I do 10 studies and I only show you the three that worked.
sentences.zh: 就像我们之前谈到的，我做了10项研究，却只向你展示了其中成功的3项。

sentences.en: Well, now, if I've pre-registered all of my studies in advance, you can find the other seven.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在如果我提前预注册了我所有的研究，你就能找到另外那7项。

sentences.en: You can say, oh, wait a second,
sentences.zh: 你可以说，哦，等一下，

sentences.en: Brian, like, is the evidence as credible as you say it is?
sentences.zh: Brian，这些证据真的像你说的那么可信吗？

sentences.en: Like, what happened to these?
sentences.zh: 这些研究怎么了？

sentences.en: And I say, oh, no, no, no, those were bad studies, you know, and you might agree or you might disagree, but at least you can see the evidence.
sentences.zh: 我会说，哦，不，不，不，那些是糟糕的研究，你知道的，你可能会同意也可能不同意，但至少你可以看到证据。

sentences.en: The other reason for pre-registration is that it makes very clear what was planned beforehand and what I discovered after the fact.
sentences.zh: 预注册的另一个原因是，它能非常清楚地说明什么是事先计划好的，什么是事后发现的。

sentences.en: And both of those modes of research are super important, right?
sentences.zh: 这两种研究模式都非常重要，对吧？

sentences.en: We have confirmatory modes of research, where it is, I have a hypothesis in advance, this theory makes these kinds of predictions, and so I'm going to
sentences.zh: 我们有验证性的研究模式，即我预先有一个假设，这个理论做出了这些预测，所以我打算

sentences.en: collect some data to test the viability of my theory, see where it holds up, see where it's weak, and then revise our confidence in the theory as a consequence.
sentences.zh: 收集一些数据来检验我理论的可行性，看看它在哪些地方站得住脚，哪些地方薄弱，并据此修正我们对该理论的信心。

sentences.en: That confirmatory part, it's really important to say in advance, how are you going to test it?
sentences.zh: 在验证性研究中，提前说明你将如何进行测试是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And so then afterwards, I don't say, oh, actually, my prediction's a little bit different, and I think it only holds here and holds there.
sentences.zh: 这样事后我就不会说，哦，实际上我的预测有点不同，我认为它只适用于这里或那里。

sentences.en: So I don't do that sort of reconstruction after the fact.
sentences.zh: 所以我不会在事后进行那种重构。

sentences.en: The other part of that is that the evidence itself becomes easier to assess because then, once I've seen the data, I am free to go into
sentences.zh: 这其中的另一个部分是，证据本身变得更容易评估，因为一旦我看到了数据，我就能自由地

sentences.en: it and explore and discover new things and find out what's in the data that might shape new ideas, might generate hypotheses for me to test next.
sentences.zh: 深入探索并发现新事物，找出数据中可能塑造新想法的内容，并可能为我接下来的测试生成假设。

sentences.en: And that's where a lot of the new discovery in science occurs, right?
sentences.zh: 而这正是科学中许多新发现产生的地方，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not from what we're testing from existing hypotheses or theories.
sentences.zh: 它不是来自我们正在测试的现有假设或理论。

sentences.en: It's when the data go totally awry and send us in a whole new direction.
sentences.zh: 而是当数据完全出乎意料，将我们引向一个全新的方向时。

sentences.en: It's like, wow, I didn't think that was going to happen.
sentences.zh: 就像是，哇，我没想到会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: And that is super important, but it's also very important to recognize that it's more uncertain.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要，但同样重要的是要认识到，这更具不确定性。

sentences.en: When data go in a different direction than expected, what we would ordinarily want to do
sentences.zh: 当数据走向与预期不同的方向时，我们通常想要做的是

sentences.en: is follow up on it, develop some hypotheses, and test those hypotheses for why it went in that new direction.
sentences.zh: 跟进它，提出一些假设，并测试这些假设，以解释为什么它会走向那个新方向。

sentences.en: So pre-registration helps keep clear when we're in these two different modes of research so that we can respect and value both of them.
sentences.zh: 因此，预注册有助于明确我们何时处于这两种不同的研究模式中，以便我们能够尊重并重视这两者。

sentences.en: So if I pre-register a study and I say I'm going to conduct these 10 experiments as part of my study, does this commit me to using all of them?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我预注册了一项研究，并说我将进行这10个实验作为我研究的一部分，这是否意味着我必须全部使用它们？

sentences.en: Or maybe I find that six out of the 10 confirm the hypothesis and the other four don't.
sentences.zh: 或者也许我发现10个中有6个证实了假设，而另外4个没有。

sentences.en: But I've told everybody that I did it.
sentences.zh: 但我已经告诉所有人我做了这些实验。

sentences.en: I mean, can I still submit the paper and leave out those four?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我还能提交论文并略过那4个吗？

sentences.en: How committed am I to including everything?
sentences.zh: 我有多大义务包含所有内容？

sentences.en: Pre-registration doesn't force you to do anything at all.
sentences.zh: 预注册并不会强迫你做任何事。

sentences.en: It just makes it so that it's transparent what it is you did.
sentences.zh: 它只是让你的所作所为变得透明。

sentences.en: So this happens all the time, right?
sentences.zh: 这种情况经常发生，对吧？

sentences.en: I plan a number of studies, I pre-register them in our lab, and then a couple of them go sideways, right?
sentences.zh: 我计划了一些研究，在实验室里预注册了它们，然后其中几个偏离了轨道，对吧？

sentences.en: Like even just implementing the study, I had a plan for how we were going to do it, and I can't do it that way.
sentences.zh: 就像在实施研究时，我有一个关于我们如何做的计划，但我无法那样做。

sentences.en: So like it is a broken study.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像是一项失败的研究。

sentences.en: But many times it's more like what you described, like it just doesn't turn out the way that I thought.
sentences.zh: 但很多时候，它更像你所描述的那样，只是结果不像我想象的那样。

sentences.en: And so I can say, well, these are the ones I'm going to report.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以说，好吧，这些是我要报告的。

sentences.en: But the value of pre-registration is in those other ones are also available.
sentences.zh: 但预注册的价值在于，其他那些研究也是可用的。

sentences.en: They're also accessible for you as a reader or for anybody in the community to say, well, I want to consider that evidence too.
sentences.zh: 作为读者或社区中的任何人，你也可以访问它们，并说，好吧，我也想考虑那些证据。

sentences.en: And so the goal of pre-registration is not to say, here are these strict rules that you now have to follow.
sentences.zh: 所以预注册的目标不是说，这里有一些你现在必须遵守的严格规则。

sentences.en: It's here is a way to articulate and make plain what your plans were and compare that to what you did.
sentences.zh: 而是提供一种方式来阐明并公开你的计划，并将其与你的实际操作进行比较。

sentences.en: And I can tell you why I had to make those changes.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你我为什么要做出这些改变。

sentences.en: Anyways, we planned to do this study with 1,000 six-month-olds to measure their attention towards this versus that.
sentences.zh: 总之，我们计划对1000名六个月大的婴儿进行这项研究，以测量他们对这个与那个的注意力。

sentences.en: Get into the study.
sentences.zh: 开始研究。

sentences.en: Turns out it's hard to do research with six-month-olds.
sentences.zh: 结果发现对六个月大的婴儿进行研究很难。

sentences.en: We thought 1,000.
sentences.zh: 我们以为是1000个。

sentences.en: That was crazy.
sentences.zh: 那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: We're going to do it with 20, right?
sentences.zh: 我们要用20个来做，对吧？

sentences.en: Whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 无论是什么情况。

sentences.en: And so at least I can then follow up and say, here's what we had to change.
sentences.zh: 所以至少我可以跟进并说，这是我们不得不改变的地方。

sentences.en: This is why we had to change it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们不得不改变它的原因。

sentences.en: And this is what we think implications it has for how confident you should be in our results.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们认为这对你应该对我们的结果有多大信心所产生的影响。

sentences.en: And then you as a reader get to say, hmm, I'm glad I can see that.
sentences.zh: 然后你作为读者可以说，嗯，我很高兴能看到这一点。

sentences.en: I'm glad I can understand how it is he got from here to there.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能理解他是如何从这里走到那里的。

sentences.en: And I either agree with his explanations and the reasons that he changed or I disagree.
sentences.zh: 我要么同意他的解释和他改变的原因，要么不同意。

sentences.en: But all of that is enabled by the transparency that pre-registration provides.
sentences.zh: 但所有这些都是由预注册提供的透明度所实现的。

sentences.en: It does not replace reasoning in any way.
sentences.zh: 它绝不会取代推理。

sentences.en: These are pretty radical changes to the way that research is being done.
sentences.zh: 这些对研究方式的改变相当激进。

sentences.en: And I'm just wondering, are these practices catching on?
sentences.zh: 我只是想知道，这些做法是否正在流行起来？

sentences.en: Are researchers agreeing, going along and saying, yeah, you know, this is what we should have been doing all along.
sentences.zh: 研究人员是否同意并随大流，说，是的，你知道，这本来就是我们一直应该做的事情。

sentences.en: I'm all in.
sentences.zh: 我完全支持。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So you opened saying that the critics have called this a reproducibility crisis.
sentences.zh: 你开场时说批评者称这为可重复性危机。

sentences.en: And I think the term is wrong.
sentences.zh: 我认为这个术语是错误的。

sentences.en: And there are many others that have said this as well, that really it's a renaissance.
sentences.zh: 还有许多其他人也这么说，这实际上是一场复兴。

sentences.en: Leif, Joe and Yuri, the ones who did that initial paper, they have a great paper recently called the psychology's renaissance.
sentences.zh: Leif、Joe和Yuri，那些完成最初那篇论文的人，最近有一篇很棒的论文，叫《心理学的复兴》。

sentences.en: And it's a very optimistic paper in that it argues that what these troubling episodes produced was of self-reflection in the
sentences.zh: 这是一篇非常乐观的论文，它认为这些令人不安的事件所产生的是心理学界对心理过程的自我反思，

sentences.en: psychological community about psychological processes, about how humans and the cultures that
sentences.zh: 关于人类以及他们所处的文化是如何

sentences.en: they inhabit are themselves influencing sometimes for the negative, but also potentially for the positive, the quality of science and how we produce and understand findings.
sentences.zh: 影响科学质量以及我们如何产生和理解发现的，有时是负面的，但也可能是正面的。

sentences.en: And so as a consequence of that, there has been a very broad engagement in the psychological community by bottom up researchers themselves saying, we need to change this.
sentences.zh: 因此，心理学界的研究人员自下而上地进行了非常广泛的参与，他们说，我们需要改变这一点。

sentences.en: And so we're going to start to adopt some of these new behaviors, sharing data, pre-registering research and otherwise, and some top down where publishers and
sentences.zh: 所以我们将开始采用一些新的行为，分享数据、预注册研究等等，还有一些自上而下的方式，出版商、

sentences.en: editors, funders, and institutions are saying, we need to change our reward systems, how it is that we encourage the most credible research that we can.
sentences.zh: 编辑、资助者和机构都在说，我们需要改变我们的奖励制度，改变我们鼓励最可信研究的方式。

sentences.en: Now it's 10 years since some of those eliciting events occur that may brought this really to the fore.
sentences.zh: 现在距离那些可能将此推向风口浪尖的诱发事件已经过去10年了。

sentences.en: And it's, you know, culture change takes a long time, but a lot has changed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，文化变革需要很长时间，但很多事情已经改变了。

sentences.en: So just as one example, we operate the open science framework.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我们运营着开放科学框架（OSF）。

sentences.en: This is part of what the Center for Open Science does is this technology where researchers can use this as a collaborative
sentences.zh: 这是开放科学中心所做工作的一部分，这项技术让研究人员可以将其用作协作

sentences.en: management service, the OSF, where you can share your data and your materials, you can pre-register your designs, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 管理服务，即OSF，你可以在这里分享你的数据和材料，预注册你的设计等等。

sentences.en: The number of users of the OSF, which is open to any discipline, not just psychology, but is more than 300,000 now since it opened in 2012, right?
sentences.zh: 自2012年开放以来，OSF的用户数量（对任何学科开放，不仅仅是心理学）现在已经超过30万了，对吧？

sentences.en: It's been increasing at exponential rates every year.
sentences.zh: 它每年都在以指数级的速度增长。

sentences.en: The number of registered studies is in the many, many thousands at this point.
sentences.zh: 目前注册的研究数量已经有成千上万了。

sentences.en: Millions of data files have been shared on the OSF.
sentences.zh: 数以百万计的数据文件已在OSF上共享。

sentences.en: And all of these show this exponential growth.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都显示出这种指数级增长。

sentences.en: And that is largely driven by the psychological community.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是由心理学界推动的。

sentences.en: And I think one of the great benefits for, of psychology confronting this is that really the challenges that are trying to be solved are psychological challenges, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为心理学面对这一挑战的一大好处是，真正试图解决的挑战是心理挑战，对吧？

sentences.en: Challenges with the individual in their behavior, challenges with the system and how individuals react to that system.
sentences.zh: 个体行为的挑战，系统以及个体如何对该系统做出反应的挑战。

sentences.en: And so as a consequence of psychology leading the way on a lot of this work, there's a lot of similar sorts of self-reflection and change happening in other disciplines.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于心理学在许多此类工作中处于领先地位，其他学科也在发生许多类似的自我反思和变革。

sentences.en: And so the reproducibility movement has spanned into biomedicine, into ecology and evolutionary biology, into the preclinical disease research, into education research and business
sentences.zh: 因此，可重复性运动已经扩展到生物医学、生态学和进化生物学、临床前疾病研究、教育研究和商业

sentences.en: research.
sentences.zh: 研究领域。

sentences.en: So that I think is going to be the real, the next 10 years is really the full embrace of these challenges across different scholarly communities.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，接下来的10年将是不同学术界全面拥抱这些挑战的时期。

sentences.en: So replicating experiments that have already been conducted isn't seen as a career enhancing move in the sciences.
sentences.zh: 所以，在科学界，重复已经进行过的实验并不被视为一种提升职业生涯的举动。

sentences.en: What, if anything, is being done in an attempt to change this, to encourage people to try to reproduce studies?
sentences.zh: 为了改变这一点，鼓励人们尝试重复研究，目前正在采取什么措施（如果有的话）？

sentences.en: Yeah, replication is an important part of science because it's how we establish the reliability of findings.
sentences.zh: 是的，重复是科学的重要组成部分，因为它是我们确立研究结果可靠性的方式。

sentences.en: We rarely do a study to make a statement about a historical fact, like did this thing happen or not?
sentences.zh: 我们很少为了陈述一个历史事实而进行研究，比如这件事是否发生过？

sentences.en: That isn't usually what a scientific hypothesis or claim would be.
sentences.zh: 这通常不是科学假设或主张的内容。

sentences.en: Often scientific claims are about if these conditions occur again, then this kind of thing will happen again sometime in the future, right?
sentences.zh: 科学主张通常是关于如果这些条件再次发生，那么这种事情在未来某个时候会再次发生，对吧？

sentences.en: We're making statements that have general application, make predictions about observations that haven't been made yet.
sentences.zh: 我们正在做出具有普遍应用价值的陈述，对尚未进行的观察做出预测。

sentences.en: Even if they're about events in the past, we haven't observed them yet.
sentences.zh: 即使它们是关于过去发生的事件，我们也还没有观察到它们。

sentences.en: The hypothesis would make an anticipation of what's going to occur.
sentences.zh: 假设会预判将要发生的事情。

sentences.en: So replication helps with assessing whether those predictions come true when you try to do them again in similar sorts of contexts as the previous research.
sentences.zh: 因此，重复有助于评估当你在与先前研究相似的环境中再次尝试时，这些预测是否成真。

sentences.en: But it is entirely valued because of those reward systems that we've been talking about focus on innovation and novelty at the expense of verification and credibility, right?
sentences.zh: 但它完全被低估了，因为我们一直在谈论的那些奖励制度以牺牲验证和可信度为代价，专注于创新和新颖性，对吧？

sentences.en: I gain more stature by having a phenomenon with my name on it, the Nosec phenomenon of X, right?
sentences.zh: 我通过拥有一个以我名字命名的现象（例如Nosec X现象）获得了更高的地位，对吧？

sentences.en: Whereas the replication is me trying to assess the credibility of somebody else's claim, usually.
sentences.zh: 而重复通常是我试图评估别人主张的可信度。

sentences.en: It could be my own, too, but isn't as valued.
sentences.zh: 它也可能是我的，但没有那么受重视。

sentences.en: So there are some things that are changing.
sentences.zh: 所以有些事情正在改变。

sentences.en: One is just a growing appreciation of the role of replication in research.
sentences.zh: 一是人们对重复在研究中作用的认识日益增强。

sentences.en: So journals are changing their policies to be more welcoming of replication studies, recognizing that it is an important contribution to science.
sentences.zh: 因此，期刊正在改变其政策，更加欢迎重复性研究，认识到这是对科学的重要贡献。

sentences.en: That opens the door.
sentences.zh: 这打开了大门。

sentences.en: It is becoming easier to do replications because researchers are sharing their materials and their data to a greater extent.
sentences.zh: 进行重复研究变得更容易了，因为研究人员在更大程度上分享了他们的材料和数据。

sentences.en: So now if someone wants to replicate somebody else's findings,
sentences.zh: 所以现在如果有人想重复别人的研究结果，

sentences.en: they can get a leg up on figuring out how they actually did their research more quickly and easily because of greater sharing.
sentences.zh: 由于共享程度的提高，他们可以更快、更容易地弄清楚别人是如何进行研究的。

sentences.en: And now there are also new publishing models that lower the barrier to trying replication studies.
sentences.zh: 现在也有了新的出版模式，降低了尝试重复研究的门槛。

sentences.en: And one of them is called registered reports.
sentences.zh: 其中之一被称为注册报告。

sentences.en: And the idea of registered reports is to really fundamentally change how is it that researchers get that key reward, the publication.
sentences.zh: 注册报告的想法是从根本上改变研究人员获得关键奖励（即发表）的方式。

sentences.en: In the standard model, I do all of my research, and then I write it up, and I submit it at the end.
sentences.zh: 在标准模式下，我完成所有的研究，然后写出来，最后提交。

sentences.en: Here are all my findings.
sentences.zh: 这是我所有的发现。

sentences.en: And then the peer reviewers evaluate whether it's credible and whether it should be published.
sentences.zh: 然后同行评审员评估它是否可信，是否应该发表。

sentences.en: In registered reports, what I submit to the journal is my plan.
sentences.zh: 在注册报告中，我提交给期刊的是我的计划。

sentences.en: Again, here's the question that I'm going to ask.
sentences.zh: 同样，这是我要问的问题。

sentences.en: Here's the background material.
sentences.zh: 这是背景材料。

sentences.en: Here's some initial evidence to say that this is worth studying.
sentences.zh: 这是初步证据，说明这值得研究。

sentences.en: And here's my study design and how I plan to analyze my data when I get it.
sentences.zh: 这是我的研究设计，以及我计划在获得数据后如何分析数据。

sentences.en: And the peer reviewers evaluate, is that an important question?
sentences.zh: 同行评审员评估，这是一个重要的问题吗？

sentences.en: And is the methodology an effective test of that question?
sentences.zh: 这种方法论是对该问题的有效测试吗？

sentences.en: And if they agree, then the journal commits to publishing my findings regardless of what happens.
sentences.zh: 如果他们同意，那么期刊承诺无论结果如何都会发表我的发现。

sentences.en: And this fundamentally changes what my goal is as the author.
sentences.zh: 这从根本上改变了作为作者我的目标。

sentences.en: Instead of my goal being make the findings as flashy, as exciting, and as innovative as possible,
sentences.zh: 我的目标不再是让研究结果尽可能华丽、令人兴奋和创新，

sentences.en: my goal is ask the most important questions and design the best methods I can to test them.
sentences.zh: 我的目标是提出最重要的问题，并设计我能做到的最好的方法来测试它们。

sentences.en: And that will get me the publication.
sentences.zh: 那就能让我发表论文。

sentences.en: And then the results are the results.
sentences.zh: 然后结果就是结果。

sentences.en: I just do the research, and then I publish whatever happens.
sentences.zh: 我只是做研究，然后无论发生什么我都发表。

sentences.en: And that changes a lot of the things that we've been talking about, right?
sentences.zh: 这改变了我们一直在谈论的许多事情，对吧？

sentences.en: It eliminates publication bias because the studies are going to get out there, whether they come the way I hoped they would or not.
sentences.zh: 它消除了发表偏倚，因为研究无论结果是否如我所愿，都会被发表出来。

sentences.en: They're all going to be reported because they've been pre-committed in advance.
sentences.zh: 它们都会被报告，因为它们是提前预承诺的。

sentences.en: They're going to get reviewed in advance, so the rigor can be enhanced compared to reviewing it afterwards, where you say, oh, well, you screwed up X, Y, and Z.
sentences.zh: 它们会被提前审查，所以严谨性可以得到提高，相比于事后审查（那时你会说，哦，你把X、Y和Z搞砸了），

sentences.en: And I say, great, well, the studies are all done.
sentences.zh: 我会说，太好了，但研究已经全部完成了。

sentences.en: I can't change that now.
sentences.zh: 我现在无法改变这一点。

sentences.en: But the relevance to replication, which is where you started in asking,
sentences.zh: 但与你开始询问的重复性的相关性在于，

sentences.en: is that it also means that I can propose to do replication studies and get commitments from the journal that they're actually interested in publishing it
sentences.zh: 这也意味着我可以提议进行重复研究，并从期刊那里获得承诺，即他们确实有兴趣发表它，

sentences.en: before I do all of the work to do the replication.
sentences.zh: 在我做所有重复工作之前。

sentences.en: And that's a lower barrier to entry, right?
sentences.zh: 这是一个更低的准入门槛，对吧？

sentences.en: I can say, well, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 我可以说，好吧，没关系。

sentences.en: I don't know if they will want the replication, but at least I can just write up a proposal for it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道他们是否想要这个重复研究，但至少我可以写一份提案。

sentences.en: And then if they don't want it, then I don't have to do it, save myself some time.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不想要，那我就不必做，节省我自己的时间。

sentences.en: So all of those are shifting some rewards for replication, but then also overall how it is people are rewarded in general.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些都在改变对重复研究的奖励，同时也改变了人们总体上获得奖励的方式。

sentences.en: Are some of these open science ideas filtering down to training yet?
sentences.zh: 这些开放科学理念是否已经渗透到培训中了？

sentences.en: I mean, are undergraduate and graduate students being taught these new methods?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，本科生和研究生是否正在学习这些新方法？

sentences.en: Yes, very much so.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常多。

sentences.en: And that's one of the more exciting elements is that that's really how these sorts of things get sustained
sentences.zh: 这是最令人兴奋的因素之一，因为这确实是这些事情得以持续的方式。

sentences.en: is where the training that gets integrated into curricula at the graduate and undergraduate levels really starts to embed these new practices.
sentences.zh: 正是这些培训，在研究生和本科生课程中真正开始将这些新实践融入其中。

sentences.en: And that's happening in formal cases like methodology instructors at their universities, building them into their coursework.
sentences.zh: 这种情况正发生在正式场合，比如大学里的方法论讲师将这些内容纳入他们的课程体系中。

sentences.en: And it's also happening in informal ways where people who are advocates for open science in the community,
sentences.zh: 这也发生在非正式场合，比如社区中那些开放科学的倡导者们，

sentences.en: and it's a very robust, lively community, are developing materials and making them available for broad dissemination.
sentences.zh: ——这是一个非常稳健且活跃的社区——他们正在开发相关材料，并使其得到广泛传播。

sentences.en: So, for example, there is a society called the Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science,
sentences.zh: 例如，有一个名为“心理科学改进协会”（Society for the Improvement of Psychological Science）的组织，

sentences.en: SIPs.
sentences.zh: 简称 SIPs。

sentences.en: It's improvingpsych.org.
sentences.zh: It's improvingpsych.org.

sentences.en: And the goal of that is to be very much of a community-based groundswell of ways that we can do better.
sentences.zh: 其目标是成为一股基于社区的强大力量，探索我们如何能做得更好。

sentences.en: And that might be creating training materials.
sentences.zh: 这可能包括创建培训材料。

sentences.en: It might be delivering training.
sentences.zh: 也可能是提供培训。

sentences.en: It might be ways to try to change some of these reward systems or anything else.
sentences.zh: 还可能是设法改变某些奖励机制或其他任何方面。

sentences.en: And that community has been fabulous at generating lots and lots of different new training materials or education devices or ways of explaining some of these challenges.
sentences.zh: 该社区在生成大量各种各样的全新培训材料、教育工具或解释这些挑战的方法方面表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: There are projects like the Fort Project or the Open Scholarship Knowledge Base
sentences.zh: 还有像“Fort项目”或“开放学术知识库”这样的项目，

sentences.en: that aggregate these materials and then make them more easily available for people to search and discover, to bring into their class or to learn themselves.
sentences.zh: 它们汇集了这些材料，使人们更容易搜索和发现，从而将其引入课堂或进行自学。

sentences.en: So that's really a big part of the engine of what is helping to sustain this change, is the community providing training for itself about these issues.
sentences.zh: 因此，社区为自身提供关于这些议题的培训，确实是推动这种变革的重要引擎。

sentences.en: Another fascinating thing that you're exploring at the center is faster ways to predict which research results are likely to replicate and which aren't.
sentences.zh: 你在中心探索的另一个引人入胜的课题是：如何更快速地预测哪些研究结果可能被复现，哪些则不能。

sentences.en: And I know you've looked at something called prediction markets and also at using artificial intelligence to predict reproducibility.
sentences.zh: 我知道你研究过所谓的“预测市场”，也研究过利用人工智能来预测可复现性。

sentences.en: Can you talk about those tools and how they work?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这些工具以及它们是如何运作的吗？

sentences.en: Doing a replication is a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 进行一次复现研究是非常耗费精力的工作。

sentences.en: So if we want to know whether a finding is trustworthy or credible, saying, okay, we've got to run it again and get all another set of participants
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们想知道一个研究发现是否值得信赖或可信，如果说“好吧，我们必须重新做一遍，找另一批参与者”，

sentences.en: and spend another year running the study and analyzing it, wow, that's a lot of effort to assess credibility.
sentences.zh: 还要再花一年时间进行研究和分析，哇，评估可信度的工作量太大了。

sentences.en: And that's essential and important and will continue to be part of the process for as long as we can envision what science will be.
sentences.zh: 这当然是必不可少且重要的，只要我们对科学的未来有所设想，它就将继续作为科学过程的一部分。

sentences.en: But it would be useful to have other indicators that gave us a more rapid assessment of the credibility of a finding, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果能有其他指标让我们更快速地评估研究发现的可信度，那不是很有用吗？

sentences.en: So peer review is supposed to provide that, but that still is a lot of effort, right?
sentences.zh: 同行评审本应提供这种评估，但这仍然需要大量的工作，对吧？

sentences.en: The reader has to read it all and decide do they think it's a credible finding or not.
sentences.zh: 读者必须通读全文，然后决定他们认为这是一个可信的发现还是其他。

sentences.en: Wouldn't it be awesome if we could have machines read the papers and decide whether those findings were credible or not?
sentences.zh: 如果能让机器阅读论文并判断这些发现是否可信，那该多棒啊？

sentences.en: And, you know, yeah, that'd be great.
sentences.zh: 你知道，是的，那会很棒。

sentences.en: Then it would be a lot less work.
sentences.zh: 那样工作量会少得多。

sentences.en: It'd be a lot faster.
sentences.zh: 速度也会快得多。

sentences.en: But, of course, can machines actually do that?
sentences.zh: 但当然，机器真的能做到吗？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: So that is sort of the goal of this program that we are part of.
sentences.zh: 所以，这正是我们参与的这个项目的目标所在。

sentences.en: And there's hundreds of collaborators involved in this program.
sentences.zh: 有数百名合作者参与了这个项目。

sentences.en: It's called SCORE.
sentences.zh: 它被称为 SCORE 项目。

sentences.en: And the idea is to see if it's possible to create algorithms, artificial intelligence, that will score papers and particular findings or claims from papers on their credibility.
sentences.zh: 其理念是看是否有可能创建算法，即人工智能，来对论文及其特定的发现或主张的可信度进行评分。

sentences.en: And if that works, then it provides an initial heuristic that readers like you or me can make about papers.
sentences.zh: 如果这行得通，它就能为像你我这样的读者提供一个初步的启发式判断依据。

sentences.en: So if I pass my own paper through the machine to say what's the scores on it,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我把自己的论文交给机器来评估得分，

sentences.en: I might learn something about where the evidence, at least from the machine's perspective, is stronger or weaker.
sentences.zh: 我可能会了解到，至少从机器的角度来看，证据在哪些地方更强或更弱。

sentences.en: And then that might help guide me for saying, oh, I need to bolster that with some additional citation evidence or other evidence that already exists.
sentences.zh: 这或许能指导我，让我意识到“哦，我需要用一些额外的引文证据或现有的其他证据来加强这一点”。

sentences.en: I might need to do another study there.
sentences.zh: 我可能需要在那里再做一项研究。

sentences.en: Or I might need to sort of look and at least look closer.
sentences.zh: 或者我可能需要仔细审视一下，至少要看得更仔细些。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You as a reviewer might do the same or as an editor might say, oh, it would be really useful to make sure we have an expert on that topic
sentences.zh: 作为审稿人，你可能会做同样的事；或者作为编辑，你可能会说：“哦，确保我们有一位该领域的专家来把关会非常有用，

sentences.en: because the machines gave an initial indication of this is an area of high uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 因为机器给出了初步迹象，表明这是一个高度不确定的领域。”

sentences.en: So that's the goal is to create some tools like that to help facilitate
sentences.zh: 所以目标就是创建这类工具，以帮助促进

sentences.en: and direct resources for the deeper dives into the evidence credibility.
sentences.zh: 并引导资源对证据的可信度进行更深入的挖掘。

sentences.en: So why do we think we can accomplish that?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们认为自己能做到这一点呢？

sentences.en: Well, there's actually some evidence that it might work.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上有一些证据表明它是可行的。

sentences.en: So the first bit of evidence is that we, in collaboration with a number of others, particularly a great group of economists, have run prediction markets
sentences.zh: 第一部分证据是，我们与许多其他人合作，特别是一群优秀的经济学家，开展了预测市场，

sentences.en: where people bet on whether findings would replicate or not.
sentences.zh: 人们在市场上押注研究发现是否能够被复现。

sentences.en: It gave them money and said you can buy shares.
sentences.zh: 给他们钱，告诉他们可以购买份额。

sentences.en: You buy a yes share.
sentences.zh: 你买“是”的份额。

sentences.en: If it succeeds in replication, you get paid.
sentences.zh: 如果复现成功，你就能获得报酬。

sentences.en: If it fails, you lose that money.
sentences.zh: 如果失败，你就损失那笔钱。

sentences.en: You buy no shares.
sentences.zh: 你买“否”的份额。

sentences.en: Then you're betting against it, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 那么你就是在与它对赌，等等。

sentences.en: And those markets were quite successful at anticipating replication outcomes when done in these systematic studies, suggesting that people have information that can anticipate
sentences.zh: 当在这些系统性研究中进行时，这些市场在预测复现结果方面非常成功，这表明人们掌握的信息可以预测

sentences.en: whether findings are likely to replicate or not.
sentences.zh: 研究发现是否可能被复现。

sentences.en: And similar findings are observed with surveys and other kinds of elicitation techniques to see, assess credibility.
sentences.zh: 在调查和其他类型的启发式技术中也观察到了类似的发现，用以评估可信度。

sentences.en: And then some, a few different teams have tried with machines, is train machines on reading papers,
sentences.zh: 然后，一些不同的团队尝试使用机器，即训练机器阅读论文，

sentences.en: give them a training set, and then give them outcomes of whether those successfully replicated or not, and then test them on with papers that have replications associated with them
sentences.zh: 给它们一个训练集，然后给出它们是否成功复现的结果，接着用机器从未见过的、带有复现结果的论文来测试它们，

sentences.en: that the machines had never seen before.
sentences.zh: 那些机器以前从未见过。

sentences.en: And they performed similarly to the humans in predicting which papers were likely to produce replicable findings and which were likely to fail to replicate.
sentences.zh: 它们在预测哪些论文可能产生可复现的发现，哪些可能复现失败方面，表现得与人类相当。

sentences.en: So those initial studies were sort of the basis of doing this project at scale, the SCORE project, which is doing this across the social behavioral sciences
sentences.zh: 因此，那些初步研究构成了大规模开展该项目的基础，即 SCORE 项目，它正在社会行为科学领域进行这项工作，

sentences.en: and involving thousands of papers and hundreds of replication studies and prediction markets and elicitations of confidence and multiple different artificial intelligence groups
sentences.zh: 涉及数千篇论文、数百项复现研究、预测市场、信心启发式评估以及多个不同的人工智能小组，

sentences.en: all trying to see if we can really create robust automated prediction of credibility.
sentences.zh: 都在努力尝试看我们是否真的能创建出稳健的自动化可信度预测。

sentences.en: And if it works, then it has lots of potential applications and lots of potential risks of overuse and inappropriate use.
sentences.zh: 如果成功了，它将具有巨大的潜在应用价值，同时也存在过度使用和不当使用的潜在风险。

sentences.en: So it'll be a very interesting challenge to navigate of how one would use these appropriately, responsibly, and effectively to help address research credibility and improve it.
sentences.zh: 因此，如何恰当、负责且有效地利用这些工具来帮助解决和提高研究可信度，将是一个非常有趣的挑战。

sentences.en: Last question for our listeners who, as I mentioned earlier, are just people who are interested in the science of psychology, not necessarily scientists or researchers themselves.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题，对于我们的听众，正如我之前提到的，他们只是对心理学科学感兴趣的人，不一定是科学家或研究人员本身。

sentences.en: How can they think about the issues that we've discussed today?
sentences.zh: 他们该如何看待我们今天讨论的这些问题？

sentences.en: Is there some way for them to know whether a paper has gone through the process of open data, open science, registration?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么方法让他们知道一篇论文是否经过了开放数据、开放科学、预注册的过程？

sentences.en: How are you getting the word out there to more of a lay audience, particularly people who just get a lot of their science by reading more popular publications,
sentences.zh: 你们是如何向更广泛的普通大众传播这些信息的？特别是那些主要通过阅读大众出版物，

sentences.en: for example, or listening to other podcasts?
sentences.zh: 或者收听其他播客来获取科学知识的人？

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it's a big challenge is how do we create effective signals of credibility for different degrees of engagement with the research finding, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实是一个巨大的挑战：我们如何为不同参与程度的研究发现创造有效的可信度信号，对吧？

sentences.en: I am a practicing scientist, and I only read a very, very tiny portion of the research literature, right?
sentences.zh: 我是一名执业科学家，但我只阅读了极小一部分的研究文献，对吧？

sentences.en: So like an everyday person, most of what I know of science, I also get through the same mechanisms, right?
sentences.zh: 所以和普通人一样，我所了解的大部分科学知识，也是通过同样的渠道获得的，对吧？

sentences.en: Reading in the newspaper or otherwise.
sentences.zh: 比如阅读报纸或其他媒体。

sentences.en: I can't read all of those papers.
sentences.zh: 我无法阅读所有那些论文。

sentences.en: There's millions of papers.
sentences.zh: 有数以百万计的论文。

sentences.en: So it is true not just for the lay person.
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅适用于普通人。

sentences.en: It's true for every person that we need more effective dissemination of the credibility, the confidence that we should have in different findings.
sentences.zh: 对于每个人来说，我们都需要更有效地传播可信度，即我们应该对不同的发现抱有多大的信心。

sentences.en: Part of that is education about how science actually works, right?
sentences.zh: 其中一部分是关于科学实际运作方式的教育，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is initial findings are always uncertain, right?
sentences.zh: 即初步发现总是存在不确定性的，对吧？

sentences.en: When that first study that comes out and says coffee is terrible for you, you know that next year of study is gonna come out and say coffee is the best thing you could ever drink.
sentences.zh: 当第一项研究出来说咖啡对你有害时，你知道明年就会有另一项研究出来说咖啡是你所能喝到的最好的东西。

sentences.en: Don't stop drinking coffee.
sentences.zh: 别停止喝咖啡。

sentences.en: And then on and on and on, right?
sentences.zh: 然后周而复始，对吧？

sentences.en: Because it's really hard to figure it out.
sentences.zh: 因为要弄清楚这一点真的很难。

sentences.en: You can't randomly assign people, you're gonna drink coffee now as the only thing you're gonna drink for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 你不能随机分配人们说：你现在开始喝咖啡，这是你余生唯一能喝的东西。

sentences.en: And you're gonna drink not coffee for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 而你余生都不喝咖啡。

sentences.en: And then we'll see who lives longer.
sentences.zh: 然后我们看看谁活得更久。

sentences.en: And you're just, the kinds of studies to actually unpack these phenomena with confidence aren't going to be done.
sentences.zh: 你根本无法进行那种能自信地剖析这些现象的研究。

sentences.en: And so the evidence accumulation for a lot of the things that we read about is slow and uncertain and subject to change.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于我们读到的许多事情，证据的积累是缓慢的、不确定的，并且容易发生变化。

sentences.en: And that's fine.
sentences.zh: 这没关系。

sentences.en: In fact, it's ordinary.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这很正常。

sentences.en: And so the one caution I think that just any of us should have is not expecting more from science than it can deliver in the short term.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们任何人都应该保持的一个谨慎态度是：不要对科学抱有超过其短期内所能提供的期望。

sentences.en: Science works on long time scales.
sentences.zh: 科学是在漫长的时间尺度上运作的。

sentences.en: And the confidence that we have is accumulation over time and building of evidence.
sentences.zh: 我们所拥有的信心是随着时间的推移和证据的积累而建立的。

sentences.en: And I shouldn't say over time necessarily.
sentences.zh: 我不应该说一定是随着时间推移。

sentences.en: It can be done very quickly with lots and lots of resource investment, right?
sentences.zh: 如果投入大量的资源，也可以很快完成，对吧？

sentences.en: COVID vaccines is a perfect example of that.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫苗就是一个完美的例子。

sentences.en: The vaccines themselves, the amount of evidence gathered in a short period of time is astonishing.
sentences.zh: 疫苗本身，在短时间内收集到的证据量是惊人的。

sentences.en: Of course, it's billions of dollars got put into making sure that we got that evidence and got it credibly very quickly.
sentences.zh: 当然，投入了数十亿美元来确保我们获得了这些证据，并非常迅速地获得了可信的证据。

sentences.en: And those particular vaccines are built on 30, 40 years of accumulated research on the basic processes of how it is that we could develop those more quickly.
sentences.zh: 而那些特定的疫苗是建立在 30、40 年积累的研究基础上的，关于我们如何能更快地开发出这些疫苗的基本过程。

sentences.en: So it feels like it happened all of a sudden, but it actually happened over many, many, many years of accumulating process and insight and evidence.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉它好像是突然发生的，但实际上它经历了许多、许多、许多年积累的过程、洞察和证据。

sentences.en: So I got a little bit off track there, but the basic point, like who can't think about COVID these days, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我有点跑题了，但基本点是，谁现在能不想到新冠呢，对吧？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: But the basic point is that just is caution, is science is slow.
sentences.zh: 但基本点就是谨慎，科学是缓慢的。

sentences.en: And so take evidence as tentative.
sentences.zh: 所以要把证据视为暂时的。

sentences.en: And the more signals that you have about transparency, the better.
sentences.zh: 关于透明度的信号越多越好。

sentences.en: And that doesn't mean that it's right.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它是正确的。

sentences.en: It does mean that it's possible that you can self-correct or obtain accurate assessments of confidence more easily.
sentences.zh: 它确实意味着你更有可能更容易地进行自我纠正或获得准确的信心评估。

sentences.en: Well, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I appreciate your talking to us today,
sentences.zh: 感谢你今天与我们交谈，

sentences.en: Dr. Nosek.
sentences.zh: Nosek 博士。

sentences.en: And I learned a lot about the renaissance that we're experiencing right now in scientific research.
sentences.zh: 我学到了很多关于我们目前在科学研究中正在经历的复兴。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Good.
sentences.zh: 很好。

sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。
